item.title: US court orders release of Cuban father held by ICE for nearly six months
item.description: A federal court in Kentucky ordered ICE to release Cuban national Damichel Jesus Viamontes Castellano after finding that authorities had detained him for nearly six months without following mandatory custody review and notice procedures.

item.title: Ohio court rules $350,000 farm sale proceeds go to heirs named in woman's will, not deed beneficiaries
item.description: In Ohio, the unexpected death of Eleanor M. Hovanick has led to a court ruling that the proceeds from her farm sale must go to her heirs as stipulated in her will. Despite having established a transfer-on-death deed for beneficiaries, the binding sale contract transformed her stake into a right to payment, altering the inheritance process.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NASA crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid in 2022; Europe's Hera probe reaches impact site to investigate if Earth can be saved from space rocks
item.description: ESA's Hera spacecraft has initiated its observations of the Didymos asteroid system following NASA's DART mission's collision with Dimorphos. This investigation seeks to analyze the impact's effects on Dimorphos' structure and its trajectory, which is essential for planetary defense. Researchers aim to uncover the momentum enhancement factor and physical effects of the collision, while also deploying CubeSats for comprehensive data collection on both asteroids.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Appeal Extends Property Dispute: Alabama Power appeals; easement case remains unresolved
item.description: A legal clash continues between Alabama Power and landowner Fenn Church over a transmission line easement. Alabama Power has appealed to the state Supreme Court after a judge refused its request for a temporary restraining order. Church is disputing the compensation for the easement while contesting the company's access to his property, as the work to construct a 74-mile transmission line faces potential delays threatening its May 2027 completion.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bearadise Halloween Attraction: Florida DIY haunt grows to 5,000 sq ft; adds Salem witch-trial history
item.description: Bearadise in Orange Park has evolved from a simple display into a beloved Halloween destination over the years. Crafted by Matt McCary, this immersive attraction features a graveyard, eerie tombstones, and haunting sound effects. With a nod to history, QR codes reveal insights about the Salem witch trials, ensuring an educational twist. This community-driven experience attracts around 250 trick-or-treaters annually, solidifying its status as a cherished neighborhood tradition.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 18th Annual Gala: Toronto event raises over $700,000; gang violence disrupts Haiti students’ schooling
item.description: Olivia Wilde's collaboration with Artists for Peace and Justice is pivotal in revolutionizing educational access for Haitian children. Following the devastating earthquake in 2010, the organization launched a free school in Port-au-Prince and now assists over 1,400 students each year. Despite ongoing gang violence hindering educational efforts, recent fundraising initiatives have generated substantial support, underscoring the vital need for continued investment in children's education and healthcare in Haiti.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nostalgic Brisbane Home Purchase: Buyer pays A$4.9m for childhood Queenslander; sale bucks weak auction market
item.description: A remarkable Queenslander residence located in Newmarket, Brisbane, was sold for A$4.9 million following an auction. The buyer, who has local roots, had no intention of bidding initially but ultimately decided to secure the property. This six-bedroom home, featuring expansive views of the city, marks a significant sale in a currently sluggish property market influenced by rising interest rates and borrowing challenges.

item.title: Montana photographer leaves 480 acres, $1 million gift to fund Alzheimer’s research in hometown after his death
item.description: Arnold Swanberg, a Montana-born photographer, donated 480 acres of farmland to the Weissman Hood Institute. The farmland will continue to be leased, and proceeds will support Alzheimer's research in Great Falls, Montana. Swanberg had personal connections to neurodegenerative diseases, influencing his decision to help research in this area. His donation is one of the largest in the institute's history and reflects his commitment to Montana.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Europe plans to heat 6,500 homes and a school using crematorium heat
item.description: Redditch Borough Council's innovative plan to use waste heat from a crematorium to warm a swimming pool is gaining traction. This project has generated significant discussions and recognition for its environmental benefits since 2013. Similar initiatives are emerging in Scotland and Finland, aiming to utilize crematoriums for heating schools and residential areas. Experts indicate this approach could be vital in addressing heating demands and reducing carbon footprints.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: For more than 20 years, Jim and Laura Currie burned and replanted their Mississippi land
item.description: For over two decades, Jim and Laura Currie have passionately worked to rejuvenate their land in Mississippi, joining forces with organizations to safeguard the endangered dusky gopher frog. In June 2026, they proudly launched a project, releasing almost 500 captive-bred frogs onto their revitalized property, with ongoing monitoring set to ensure these frogs flourish in their new home.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: This one single habit at night was linked to a 20 to 30 per cent higher rate of fatty liver disease and cirrhosis in a US study of nearly 200,000 adults followed for decades by Oregon researchers.
item.description: An intriguing study reveals that eating late at night can negatively impact liver health, contributing to greater risks of liver-related illnesses. Participants consuming late meals showed elevated instances of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and cirrhosis. By examining data from nearly 200,000 adults, researchers advocate for maintaining consistent meal timing to support the liver's functionality and align with natural bodily cycles.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Frenchman finds €700,000 worth of gold while digging pool in backyard
item.description: A homeowner in Neuville-sur-Saône found 5 gold bars and hundreds of coins during pool excavation. While the treasure was valued at approximately €700,000, its origins remained a mystery. Investigations confirmed the gold had been legally acquired and was not tied to any crime. Authorities determined the homeowner could retain the gold as it held no archaeological importance. The previous owner's death left unanswered questions regarding the gold's burial.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US Senator Chris Van Hollen announces bid to replace Schumer as Democratic leader
item.description: Chris Van Hollen has declared his intention to run for the Senate Majority Leader position against Chuck Schumer. He argues that the Democratic Party needs new leadership to better address voter desires for change. Support for Van Hollen's bid has come from influential figures like Bernie Sanders and Abdul El-Sayed. Meanwhile, Schumer maintains his confidence in retaining his leadership role amid ongoing discussions.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Researchers on 28 Peruvian cacao farms found birds and bats nearly doubled harvests by pest control
item.description: A recent study highlights the vital role of wildlife, particularly birds and bats, in managing pests on cacao farms. These creatures enhance cacao production, especially in areas rich in trees, leading to improved farmer profits. However, for farmers to maximize these benefits, preserving diverse habitats and effectively managing tree growth to ensure adequate light for cacao trees is essential.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: A dead star called J1328-1450 is circled by two separate rings of shattered planets
item.description: In a groundbreaking discovery, astronomers have identified two unique gaseous rings encircling the white dwarf star J1328-1450. Utilizing the Very Large Telescope in Chile, researchers explored the surrounding materials, indicating that some smaller planetary bodies likely survived the star's catastrophic end. Unlike previous findings, these rings display varied chemical compositions, shedding light on the planetary conditions that existed prior to the star's demise.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
